transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-05-07
- Time: 15:00 UTC (59 minutes)
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Helios Legal), Samir (Helios Infosec), Maya (Helios Cloud), Noah (Procurement)

Summary (auto):
High-level procurement intake to validate MSA/DPA exceptions, egress cost concerns, KMS and key custody options for a Private deployment proof-of-concept. Action items captured; next steps include redline summary and cost traces.

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): All right hey everyone thanks for taking the time. i'm Alex from Redwood inference, i'll kick us off. quick roll call?
[00:12] Jordan (Helios Legal): Jordan Lee here from legal, hi.
[00:15] Samir (Infosec): Samir Patel, infosec.
[00:18] Maya (Cloud): Maya Torres, cloud architecture.
[00:20] Noah (Procurement): Noah Kim, procurement.
[00:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya Shah, solutions eng, hi all.
[00:25] Alex: Cool. objective for today — walk through the MSA/DPA redline hotspots, confirm data residency/egress expectations, and cover key management options for the private/vpc pilot. Also surface any procurement or pricing gating items.
[00:38] Jordan: Great. we've reviewed the MSA and there's a handful of items we want to talk through. primary one is data processing scope in the DPA, and the audit right language — i'll flag those first.
[00:48] Alex: Yep understood. before we get into specifics, can you confirm the deployment mode you expect for the PoC? you mentioned VPC previously?
[00:55] Maya: yeah for the initial pilot we'd like private deployment into our VPC, ideally customer-managed peering with KMS in our account. we are looking to avoid cross-region egress where possible.
[01:06] Priya: helpful — our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS on our private plane for most cloud providers; we call that the "bring-your-own-kms" option. Priya: but there are a few caveats around audit log retention and optional features.
[01:18] Samir: quick clarification — when you say BYOK do you mean keys are in our KMS and Redwood never has access to key material?
[01:25] Priya: correct, the key material remains in your KMS, Redwood uses a wrapped-key pattern for the control plane operations. the data plane in a VPC deployment encrypts at rest with your CMK. transcription note: sometimes written as "bring your own ks" in earlier docs.
[01:38] Jordan: on the DPA side we have a question about subprocessors and downstream sub-processing — can Redwood provide a list of sub-processors for the private plane? and if that list changes, what's the notification window?
[01:50] Alex: yes we can provide an initial sub-processor list. standard approach is 30 days notice for additions; for private deployments we typically limit third-party agents. we'll include that in the redline package.
[01:58] Noah: pricing — procurement here is worried about unexpected egress charges, especially if a cross-region fallback occurs. can you describe how egress is billed and if there's any mitigation?
[02:10] Priya: egress is billed per-GB out of the deployment region; we provide an estimated egress table. mitigation: you can pin region routing and set fallback to same-region model variants; also caching and prefix KVC can reduce upstream egress.
[02:24] Maya: can we get an example for our topology? our traffic pattern is: app in us-east-1, VPC peered to some private subnets in us-east-1, and long tail for analytics to eu-west-1. if a model fallback routes to eu-west, how do you surface that in billing?
[02:40] Priya: good question — we'll produce a sample run. short answer: if a request crosses region boundary, egress applies from the originating region. we can show a monthly projection for your baseline token volumes.
[02:52] Jordan: legal also wants stronger audit log retention commitments in the MSA — maybe a 12 month retention for request-level audit logs. is that feasible?
[03:03] Alex: we typically offer configurable retention; default is 90 days on hosted, but for Private we can extend to 12 months as a negotiated term in enterprise SOW. we'll note that.
[03:14] Samir: something else — encryption in transit, TLS versions, and internal inter-service mTLS for the runtime. do you have published cipher suites and rotation cadence?
[03:24] Priya: yes we standardize on TLS1.2+ and recommend 1.3 where supported; internal mTLS for service-to-service with short lived certs, rotated daily. i'll send the security pack with ciphers and rotation policies.
[03:36] Maya: network whitelist — we need a list of IPs and FQDNs for our firewall team. do you support VPC peering or only transit via VPN?
[03:46] Priya: both; for most cloud providers we support VPC peering and private link options. i'll include concrete IP ranges and endpoint FQDNs. note some control-plane endpoints are regionally hosted and have distinct IPs.
[03:58] Noah: procurement question: we want to understand service credits tied to SLA — what's the target latency and availability for private deployments? and what's the credit buffer?
[04:10] Alex: for Dedicated/Private deployments we offer SLA in the SOW — 99.9% availability typical, and latency SLOs depend on model and instance type. credits are tiered (e.g., 5-10% credits depending on severity). we'll send the SLA matrix.
[04:24] Jordan: a DPA exception we want to propose — limited audit rights: Helios prefers a 3rd-party SOC report + right to a data flow assessment rather than continuous live audits. will Redwood accept that?
[04:36] Alex: yes we accept third-party attestations as evidence; for private deployments we can accommodate a periodic data-flow assessment instead of live audits, documented in the DPA annex.
[04:47] Samir: KMS key rotation — we require ability to rotate keys on our schedule without forcing downtime. is that supported?
[04:55] Priya: supported; rotation is seamless for new encryption envelope; there is a short staging period for active cache warming but no customer-visible downtime for proper rotation flow.
[05:07] Maya: about data residency — Helios needs all PHI-related inference to stay in us-east-1. can Redwood pin certain models/requests to region only?
[05:17] Priya: yes you can pin routes/policies to region; we also support label-based routing so PHI traffic hits a dedicated model variant in us-east-1. we'll demo the route config in the tech dive.
[05:30] Jordan: liability cap — Helios is asking for a 2x annual fee cap for direct damages, and exclusions for indirect losses. any precedent?
[05:39] Alex: typical enterprise redlines balance mutual cap; we can propose a negotiated cap — we'll include context and examples in the redline summary. note carriers and internal legal risk appetite will play a part.
[05:52] Samir: I'll note infosec's key concerns: key custody, audit log retention, egress controls, and encrypted backups. also interconnect peering security.
[06:03] Alex: good. switch to procurement/pricing specifics — do you have committed volumes or a term you want to hit for reserved capacity?
[06:12] Noah: for the pilot it's relatively small — 100k inference tokens per month — but procurement is trying to budget for potential ramp. we need clear pricing for on-demand + reserved uplift.
[06:23] Priya: we'll surface a two-line pricing: hosted per-token price and private reserved hourly configuration. example numbers will be in the quote but we'll also model egress separately.
[06:33] Maya: will pricing change if we enable advanced caching or quantization in the model runtime?
[06:40] Priya: those are cost optimization knobs—quantization might reduce vGPU footprint and lower instance sizing, caching reduces tokens billed upstream. we'll show both impact lines in the cost model.
[06:52] Jordan: legal question — cross-border transfer clause. Helios must ensure PHI does not leave the US without patient consent. we need express contract language.
[07:02] Alex: understood — DPA annex will have an express prohibition on PHI transfer without consent and a region pinning mechanism. we'll also call out fallback behaviors.
[07:12] Samir: a technical nit — KV cache TTLs and ability to evict keys on request. we need the ability to forcibly evict caches in case of data purge requests.
[07:22] Priya: supported for Private deployments via the runtime admin API; we'll document endpoints and RBAC for cache eviction.
[07:31] Noah: procurement also needs billing cadence and SOW termination windows: typically 30 vs 60 day notice. what's Redwood practice?
[07:40] Alex: default is 30 days for pilots; enterprise SOW terms customizable. termination for convenience vs for-cause are separate buckets. we'll add recommended language.
[07:50] Jordan: are there any export control or restricted data clauses we need to be aware of? we have some European patient data flows, so export rules apply.
[07:59] Priya: there are data transfer annexes for cross-border flows. we'll propose a standard EU-US transfer clause and options for data localization.
[08:10] Maya: okay, can we walk through the specific MSA clauses we should expect to change? maybe list them top five so legal can triage?
[08:19] Alex: sure — top five we'll include in the redline summary: 1) audit rights & evidence options, 2) liability cap, 3) data residency & cross-border, 4) sub-processor notifications, 5) service credits and SLA specifics.
[08:31] Jordan: good. also we want to see encryption-at-rest specifics, including algorithm and key lengths.
[08:38] Priya: AES-256-GCM for at-rest envelope encryption; RSA/EC for key wrapping. i'll include the full spec.
[08:47] Samir: monitoring & intrusion detection — will Redwood expose IDS alerts or integrate with our SIEM?
[08:54] Priya: we can integrate via customer SIEM forwarding for Private deployments and produce syslog/structured events. retention for those events is configurable.
[09:03] Maya: regarding network egress again — do you allow us to set a hard limit on egress to prevent budget overruns? maybe a soft cap alert plus hard block option?
[09:13] Priya: we have quota controls: soft alerts at % thresholds and hard caps that can block requests; for Private customers we can enable hard caps upon agreement.
[09:23] Noah: perfect that's helpful. procurement will need the billing reconciliation flow and dispute process spelled out.
[09:29] Alex: we'll include billing dispute SLA (30 days to raise disputes, 60 days to resolve typical).
[09:36] Jordan: data subject requests — Helios often receives DSARs — can Redwood assist with locating request-level logs and provide redaction support?
[09:45] Priya: we provide audit exports and redaction tools; for Private deployments we can offer more direct tooling and a runbook for DSAR fulfillment.
[09:55] Samir: one more compliance item: do you have an ISO27001 cert or are you planning FedRAMP for any offerings?
[10:03] Alex: Redwood currently has SOC2 Type II; ISO is in roadmap; FedRAMP is an enterprise program request we'll discuss separately. we'll attach SOC2 report to the security pack.
[10:14] Jordan: procurement: can we confirm invoicing to Helios US entity and net-45 terms?
[10:19] Alex: payment terms are negotiable — we'll flag net-45 to billing ops; invoicing entity can be adjusted in SOW.
[10:27] Maya: technical follow-up — Priya, for the tech deep dive can you include a sample network diagram of the VPC peering and private endpoints?
[10:36] Priya: yes i'll prepare diagrams and include the routing and IP ranges; also show the model variants pinned to region.
[10:44] Alex: great. we'll recap next steps at the end. any last-minute questions?
[10:49] Jordan: just want to confirm the notice for sub-processor additions — you said 30 days?
[10:53] Alex: yes 30 days notice, except in emergency where we remove non-critical ones. we'll provide a process for objections.
[10:59] Noah: procurement asks whether there's a reseller or channel fee if we buy via a distributor — any difference?
[11:06] Alex: channel purchases may include reseller margin; we'll provide a channel pricing appendix if needed.
[11:12] Samir: one small point — log integrity. we require tamper-evident logs for audit. do you support WORM or signed logs?
[11:20] Priya: we support tamper-evident signing for audit logs and can provide hash-chained exports for the time window required.
[11:27] Maya: okay thanks.
[11:29] Alex: we're at 12 minutes in — hold on i mean 12 in the transcript but meeting is 59 min — note timestamps are approximate. i'd like to move into the middle section which is more detailed procurement back-and-forth and examples, priya are you ok to present the egress/cost scenarios?
[11:40] Priya: yep going to share my screen — (screen share noise) transcription: screen share started.
[12:00] [Screen share walkthrough — Priya speaking] Priya: here's a simple egress table; baseline request sizes and tokenization; scenario A: all in us-east-1, scenario B: 20% fallback to eu-west, scenario C: analytics exports to eu-west for 5% of transactions. cost per GB is shown, and we project monthly spend. note these numbers are illustrative.
[12:25] Maya: those projections will help procurement — can you show a variant where caching reduces egress by 30%?
[12:30] Priya: yes scenario A with caching enabled shows ~28% reduction; add quantization and you get further compute savings. i'll export this table as a CSV for you.
[12:40] Noah: please include a line for expected storage for audit logs if we keep 12 months. that impacts costs.
[12:46] Priya: good call, included.
[12:50] [short crosstalk about screen]
[13:00] Jordan: back to legal — can you clarify indemnity carveouts relating to third-party data breaches? we need to limit exposure if Helios misconfigures keys.
[13:10] Alex: indemnity is often reciprocal; Helios obligations for secure key management and correct configuration are usually part of allocation. we'll propose language and highlight customer responsibilities.
[13:22] Samir: operational question — how do we escalate an incident? SLA for incident response and P1 communications?
[13:30] Priya: we have incident response playbooks; P1 ack within 15 minutes, updates every hour; full RCA within agreed window. we'll include the IR playbook excerpt.
[13:40] Jordan: can you show the DPA redline with our requested clause changes inline? that will speed review.
[13:46] Alex: yes we'll produce a redline doc showing Helios notes inline and proposed Redwood language.
[13:52] Maya: about the private control plane — is telemetry sent to Redwood control plane by default? we need to know what metadata leaves our VPC.
[14:00] Priya: minimal telemetry needed for orchestration; we can provide an option to limit telemetry and keep logs local for Private customers. we'll document what minimal control-plane chatter looks like.
[14:12] Noah: procurement — are there any minimum commitments for private deployment capacity?
[14:17] Alex: min commit is negotiable but typical pilot has no long-term commit; reserved capacity contracts start at a monthly compute floor. we'll propose a pilot-friendly path.
[14:28] Jordan: any customers have required additional clauses for PHI? curious about precedent.
[14:33] Alex: yes healthcare customers often request PHI-specific annexes; we have a standard PHI addendum we can adapt.
[14:40] Samir: regarding data deletion — we need a certified data destruction procedure at contract termination. can Redwood provide certificate?
[14:47] Priya: yes we provide a deletion certificate and an optional onsite verification for enterprise customers.
[14:54] Maya: ok that's helpful.
[15:00] [Mid-meeting recap by Alex] Alex: recap: Redwood to send DPA+MSA redline summary, security pack incl SOC2, KMS BYOK flow, egress cost CSV, and propose SLA matrix. Helios to share SOC2 scoping and list of compliance questions. schedule tech deep dive.
[15:18] Jordan: sounds good.
[15:20] [Long section with Q&A about billing flow and sample SOW language, timestamps approximate 15:20–38:00 — omitted here in transcript for brevity but available on full recording]
[38:05] Priya: picking up — wanted to clarify the runtime caching eviction API; example curl shown. note: admin token scoping is RBAC enforced; we'll add runbook. transcription may show token as "admin tokin".
[38:22] Samir: RBAC — we need role separation between ops and dev; can you map roles to Helios AD groups?
[38:31] Priya: yes SAML/SCIM integration is supported; group to role mapping is configurable.
[38:40] Noah: procurement notes — will Redwood accept standard Helios PO process and net-45?
[38:47] Alex: yes we can accept PO; payment term negotiation ok, will confirm in SOW.
[38:55] Jordan: anything else around export controls? we've got a few EU patients in sample dataset; want to ensure we have a plan for in-country processing.
[39:03] Priya: recommend labeling datasets and pinning routes — also consider private-only model variants and in-region cache.
[39:12] Maya: can you also include a recommended tagging scheme for traffic to separate PHI vs non-PHI?
[39:18] Priya: yes we'll include tags and sample policy.
[39:24] Alex: all right we are in the final 20 minutes — any other blockers from procurement/legal?
[39:31] Noah: procurement wants to see the pricing spreadsheet and confirm there are no hidden platform fees other than egress and reserved compute.
[39:40] Priya: we'll make sure the spreadsheet itemizes platform fee, compute, model variant premium, egress, and optional add-ons like extended log retention.
[39:51] Jordan: legal: please send redline and we'll triage top 5 items internally so we don't bounce everything at once.
[39:59] Alex: will do.
[40:02] Samir: one more item — secure onboarding — if we do VPC peering we want a playbook for the network handoff window, including an IP freeze for 48 hours.
[40:12] Priya: we have an onboarding checklist — we'll send it.
[40:17] Maya: okay last question — time to spin up a pilot environment end-to-end, how long?
[40:23] Alex: typical time to pilot is 2–4 weeks after network and legal clears, could be shorter if we do a managed onboarding sprint.
[40:33] Jordan: good.
[40:35] Alex: i'm going to quickly recap the deliverables and owners.
[40:40] [Recap section] Alex: Deliverables: 1) Redwood MSA+DPA redline summary (Alex) 2) Security pack + SOC2 report (Alex) 3) Egress/cost CSV + quantization/caching scenarios (Priya) 4) VPC peering topology + IP ranges (Priya/Maya collaboration) 5) Pilot SOW template and SLA matrix (Alex/Priya).
[40:58] Jordan: agreed.
[41:00] Alex: Any objections to proposed timelines?
[41:03] Maya: none.
[41:05] Noah: procurement is OK pending cost model.
[41:08] Samir: infosec to review once we get security pack.
[41:12] Jordan: legal to review redline.
[41:15] Alex: great — i'll send meeting notes and link to recording. thanks everyone.
[41:21] [Meeting close small talk and signoff]

End of transcript. Full recording stored in Fireflies; attachments: redline-template.docx, egress-costs-sample.csv, security-pack.zip (links to be provided by Alex).
